prompt.zh-TW: 小晴開了一家「小山咖啡」。開店第一個月底，店裡有一台義式咖啡機、一批還沒用完的咖啡豆，銀行戶頭裡也還有一些錢。這三樣東西在帳上都屬於哪一類？
prompt.en: Ching has opened Hillside Coffee. At the end of the first month the shop has an espresso machine, a stock of unused coffee beans and some money in the bank. Which class do all three belong to in the books?

text.zh-TW: 資產：都是店裡擁有、之後能帶來好處的資源
text.en: Assets: all are resources the shop owns and expects to benefit from

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。能賣咖啡的機器、能做成飲料的豆子、能付帳的現金，都是資產。
feedback.en: That's right. A machine that makes coffee, beans that become drinks and cash that pays the bills are all assets.

text.zh-TW: 只有銀行裡的錢是資產，機器和豆子不是
text.en: Only the money in the bank is an asset; the machine and beans are not

feedback.zh-TW: 你把現金放對地方了。不過資產不只現金：咖啡機與咖啡豆也是店裡擁有、之後會帶來好處的東西，一樣是資產。
feedback.en: You placed the cash correctly. Assets are more than cash, though: the machine and the beans are also things the shop owns that will bring future benefit, so they are assets too.

text.zh-TW: 負債：買這些東西都花了錢
text.en: Liabilities: buying these things cost money

feedback.zh-TW: 花了錢買東西，錢變成了另一種資產，不是欠別人錢。負債是公司還沒付、將來要付給別人的款項。
feedback.en: Spending cash on something turns it into a different asset; it does not create a debt. Liabilities are amounts still owed to others.

explanation.zh-TW: 判斷資產的方法是問：這是店裡擁有、之後能帶來好處的東西嗎？咖啡機、咖啡豆、現金都是，所以答案是{{option:o_80gh}}。{{option:o_60qb}}把資產想得太窄；{{option:o_xx5r}}把「花過錢」和「欠別人錢」混在一起了。
explanation.en: To spot an asset, ask: does the shop own this, and will it bring future benefit? The machine, the beans and the cash all qualify, so the answer is {{option:o_80gh}}. {{option:o_60qb}} takes too narrow a view of assets, and {{option:o_xx5r}} confuses having spent money with owing money.
